$comment: ADR-037 register fragment (seed-whatsapp-bsp-source). Seeds the pre-built `whatsapp-bsp` OpenConnector source consumed by the OpenRegister outbound-messaging dispatch leaf (MessageDispatchProvider) and, transitively, pipelinq's WhatsAppProviderClient (BSP-fallback leg). This is the generic Business Solution Provider relay slot — modelled on CM.com's WhatsApp Business API, which authenticates with an `X-CM-PRODUCTTOKEN` request header and accepts a Meta-shaped messages payload. MOCK MODE (integration-mock-mode): ships with `configuration.mock:true` + a realistic `configuration.mockResponse` (Meta-shaped messages reply, a mock `wamid.MOCK-BSP-0001` id) and isEnabled:true, so the dispatch leaf is demonstrably functional end-to-end WITHOUT a BSP credential — the OpenRegister ExternalIntegrationRouter short-circuits the mock-flagged source and returns the canned success body WITHOUT sending a WhatsApp message. To go live: repoint `location` at your chosen BSP (e.g. Twilio Content API, 360dialog, MessageBird WhatsApp), set the matching credential header (default models CM.com `X-CM-PRODUCTTOKEN`), and REMOVE `configuration.mock`. The base URL is admin-owned on the source (no SSRF surface). OUTBOUND (side-effecting POST) — template-approval gating, the 24h session window, provider selection (Meta-primary, this BSP as fallback), STOP opt-out, dedupe and delivery-status reconciliation all stay in the consuming app (pipelinq WhatsAppAdapter); this source is a pure transport.
